holidays.name: Independence Day
holidays.description: The big American fireworks bash, where millions of people grill meat, wave flags, and set off things that go boom in the name of freedom. Hot dogs, watermelon, and sparklers are practically mandatory.
holidays.origin: Marks the adoption of the Declaration of Independence by the Continental Congress in 1776, when the thirteen colonies declared their separation from Great Britain. It became a federal holiday in 1870.
holidays.funFact: Congress actually voted for independence on July 2, 1776, and John Adams predicted that July 2 would be the day celebrated forever. Americans have been celebrating two days later ever since.

holidays.name: Nathan's Hot Dog Eating Contest
holidays.description: A gloriously absurd competitive eating spectacle at Coney Island, where contestants race to cram as many hot dogs and buns as possible into their mouths in ten minutes.
holidays.origin: Legend says it began in 1916 when four immigrants settled an argument over who was the most patriotic by seeing who could eat the most hot dogs. Historians say the story was a publicity invention, and the contest has been documented since the 1970s.
holidays.funFact: Joey Chestnut has won the contest many times, including a record 76 hot dogs and buns in 10 minutes in 2021.

holidays.name: National Barbecue Day
holidays.description: An unofficial food holiday on which people fire up the grill and celebrate smoky, charred, sauce-slathered goodness, which overlaps nicely with the Independence Day cookout.
holidays.origin: A food-industry and foodie observance that grew from the American tradition of Fourth of July cookouts, with no single official founder.
holidays.funFact: Barbecue and Independence Day have been linked since colonial times. George Washington reportedly attended a barbecue in 1769 and wrote about it in his diary.

holidays.name: National Caesar Salad Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the crunchy, garlicky, anchovy-kissed salad that somehow became a restaurant staple around the world.
holidays.origin: Said to have been invented on July 4, 1924, by restaurateur Caesar Cardini in Tijuana, Mexico, when a holiday rush emptied his kitchen and he improvised with what was left.
holidays.funFact: The original recipe reportedly had no anchovies. The anchovy flavor was said to come from Worcestershire sauce.

holidays.name: Independence from Meat Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek vegetarian counter-celebration inviting people to declare independence from meat on the biggest grilling day of the year.
holidays.origin: Started by vegetarian and animal advocacy circles as a playful twist on Independence Day, encouraging people to try plant-based cookouts.
holidays.funFact: Plant-based hot dogs and burgers have become more common at Fourth of July cookouts, putting this observance in direct, friendly competition with Nathan's hot dog contest.
